title: appwrite/appwrite offers a self-hostable backend for agents and applications
friendlyTitle: Appwrite provides one open backend for apps and AI agents
summary: Appwrite is a widely used open-source backend covering authentication, databases, storage, functions, messaging, hosting and realtime services. Its current release and recent changes include MCP and command-line activity support, making the platform relevant to both conventional applications and agent-operated workflows.
friendlySummary: Appwrite combines login, databases, files, functions, messages, hosting and live updates in one open-source platform. Recent work also makes activity from MCP tools and command lines easier to see.
whyItMatters: Teams can self-host common application services instead of wiring each capability from scratch, while keeping agent activity close to the same permissions and data controls used by the rest of the product. Its broad scope means deployment, upgrades and security still require deliberate operational ownership.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Developers can reuse one backend for normal app features and agent workflows. Self-hosting gives more control, but the team must still manage updates, backups and security.
